title: Police called racist; Professor backs up Dumas family
article: Racism among Winnipeg police is the reason Matthew Dumas was shot and killed by a cop, the victim's family charged yesterday following a two-week inquest into the death 3.5 years ago.

Jessica Dumas, a sister of the 18-year-old aboriginal man who was shot while wielding a screwdriver on a North End street, joined her mother, First Nations officials and a University of Manitoba sociology professor in slamming city police for what they claimed is a practice of "racial profiling" of suspects.
"Matthew shouldn't have been killed," Jessica Dumas told reporters at the Southern Chiefs Organization's offices after the completion of the inquest into the Jan. 31, 2005 incident.
"It's beyond unfortunate that we'll never get to hear Matthew's side of the story."
It was the first time Matthew's family had spoken publicly about the incident since the inquest began.

Jessica echoed an argument made at the inquest by her family's lawyer Donald Worme, insisting that her brother -- after having been pepper-sprayed by an officer -- did not "lunge" at one of the cops who had surrounded him on Dufferin Avenue while looking for suspects in a robbery.
Worme had told the inquest, headed by provincial court Judge Mary Curtis, that Matthew had only been wiping his eyes to relieve pain from the spray.
"Matthew refused to comply. That much I can agree with," Jessica said. "But there's a difference between refusing to comply and lunging."

Despite the inquest's revelation that Matthew Dumas had initially run from cops on the street because of a warrant for his arrest for a separate, previous investigation, sociology professor Elizabeth Comack -- who studies criminology, inner-city policing and aboriginals -- said "race had everything to do" with his death.
She added that a "full understanding" of social conditions for urban natives is needed for the wider community to see that.
"It's pretty clear that any fear and distrust that Matthew might have had about police was actually well-founded," said Comack. "Because he did, after all, end up being shot to death."
The inquest had heard that Matthew Dumas had lunged at Const. Dennis Gburek with the screwdriver and was then shot twice.
An RCMP expert on use-of-force practices had testified that Gburek followed proper procedure when firing the shots.
However, Nahanni Fontaine, the SCO's justice director, said Dumas would not have been shot if he had been white instead of aboriginal.
She argued that his death is "parallel to what happened with J.J. Harper" when that native man was shot and killed by a city cop on Logan Avenue in March 1988.
